resources.string:
Initializes the ATOM SDK singleton, asks for the system VPN permission if it has not been granted yet, and opens the dashboard.

SDK call:
AtomManager.initialize(context, atomConfiguration, InitializeCallback)

How to use: build atomConfiguration with new AtomConfiguration.Builder(ATOM_SECRET_KEY).build(); the ready AtomManager arrives in InitializeCallback.onInitialized(). In this demo it runs from AtomDemoApplicationController.onCreate(). The username and password entered here are applied later with atomManager.setVPNCredentials(new VPNCredentials(username, password)) right before connect(). The permission comes from VpnService.prepare(context).
Shows or hides the VPN password.\n\nNo SDK call - UI only. The password is handed to the SDK as new VPNCredentials(username, password) via atomManager.setVPNCredentials() before each connect().

Clears the username and password fields.\n\nNo SDK call - UI only. Nothing has been sent to the SDK yet; credentials are only applied with atomManager.setVPNCredentials() when a connection is started.

Opens Connection With Params and selects it (the default) for the Connection tab: dial a country or city with up to three protocols.

SDK calls:
new VPNProperties.Builder(country or city, primaryProtocol)
.withSecondaryProtocol() / .withTertiaryProtocol()
atomManager.connect(context, vpnProperties)

How to use: fetch the inventory with getProtocols(), getCountries() and getCities(), pick from it, build VPNProperties and call connect().

Opens Connection With Channel and selects it for the Connection tab: dial a streaming channel instead of a location.

SDK calls:
atomManager.getChannels(CollectionCallback)
new VPNProperties.Builder(channel, primaryProtocol)
atomManager.connect(context, vpnProperties)

How to use: pick a Channel from getChannels() that supports your protocols, build VPNProperties with it and call connect().

Opens Connection With Multiple Dedicated IPs and selects it for the Connection tab: dial one of several hosts reserved for this user.

SDK calls:
new DedicatedDNS() per host
new VPNProperties.Builder(dedicatedDNSList, protocol)
atomManager.connect(context, vpnProperties)

How to use: fill a DedicatedDNS for each host (name, IP, protocol, port), pass the list with an optional preferred protocol, build VPNProperties and call connect().

Opens Connection With Dedicated IP and selects it for the Connection tab: dial a host reserved for this user.

SDK calls:
new VPNProperties.Builder(dedicatedHost, protocol)
atomManager.connect(context, vpnProperties)

How to use: pass the dedicated IP or host name as a String together with a Protocol, build VPNProperties and call connect().

Dashboard: SDK state and the three ways to connect.

SDK calls:
atomManager.getCurrentVpnStatus(context)
AtomManager.addVPNStateListener(listener)

How to use: read getCurrentVpnStatus() once for the current state, then keep it current from the VPNStateListener callbacks.
Connection: opens the connect screen selected on the Dashboard - Params, Channel or Dedicated IP. Connect with Params is selected by default.\n\nNo SDK call.

Locations: the SDK inventory as a searchable server list.

SDK calls:
atomManager.getCountries()
atomManager.getOptimizedCountries()
atomManager.getRecommendedCountry()

How to use: getCountries() lists every location, getOptimizedCountries() adds measured latency and getRecommendedCountry() gives the SDK's best pick for this user.
More: protocol, split tunneling, logs, security features and SDK info.\n\nNo SDK call to open it; each row explains its own call when held.

Measures the latency to every country and shows it as the ping on each card. Needs pings to get through; on failure the readings stay as they were.

SDK call:
atomManager.getOptimizedCountries(CollectionCallback)

How to use: the call is asynchronous and answers on its callback's onSuccess(), onError() or onNetworkError().

Reloads the server list and each country's cities. Latencies already measured are kept; the recommended location is not refreshed.

SDK calls:
atomManager.getCountries(CollectionCallback)
atomManager.getCities(CollectionCallback)

How to use: each call is asynchronous and answers on its callback's onSuccess(), onError() or onNetworkError().

Switches the demo between light and dark theme and remembers the choice. Until it is first used the demo follows the system setting.\n\nNo SDK call: this is the app\'s own AppCompatDelegate night mode.

Opens SDK Logs: everything the demo and the SDK have reported, with a level filter.\n\nHow to use: the SDK reports through the callbacks of each call and VPNStateListener; the demo records those in its LogStore.

Lists this country's cities underneath; tap again to hide them. Each city connects on its own, with the city's recommended protocol.

SDK calls:
country.getCities()
new VPNProperties.Builder(city, city.getRecommendedProtocol())

How to use: getCountries() already carries each country's cities, so no extra call is needed.

Opens Connection With Params with this country selected and its recommended protocol as primary, then connects - the same as picking it there and tapping Connect. If a VPN is already up it only preselects, so you can Disconnect or use COC.

SDK calls:
new VPNProperties.Builder(country, country.getRecommendedProtocol())
atomManager.connect(context, vpnProperties)

How to use: any Country from getCountries() can go straight into VPNProperties.Builder.

Opens Connection With Params with the SDK's recommended location selected, then connects.

SDK calls:
atomManager.getRecommendedCountry(Callback)
new VPNProperties.Builder(country, country.getRecommendedProtocol())
atomManager.connect(context, vpnProperties)

How to use: getRecommendedCountry() returns a Country you can pass straight to VPNProperties.Builder.
Goes back to the previous screen.\n\nNo SDK call - UI only.
Clears the log list.\n\nNo SDK call - the list is this demo\'s own store. It is filled from the callbacks of a VPNStateListener registered with AtomManager.addVPNStateListener(listener).

Pauses or resumes recording new log entries.\n\nNo SDK call - it only stops this demo\'s store taking entries. To stop receiving SDK events altogether, call AtomManager.removeVPNStateListener(listener).
Copies the visible log entries to the clipboard.\n\nNo SDK call - UI only.
Filters the list by level.\n\nNo SDK call. Levels map onto VPNStateListener callbacks: onConnected() is success, onRedialing() a warning, onDialError() an error, and state changes are info.

The protocol the connect screens start with as primary. It can still be changed there for each connection.

SDK call:
atomManager.getProtocols(CollectionCallback)

How to use: the SDK has no global protocol setting - pass one per connection to new VPNProperties.Builder(location, protocol). This demo keeps the preferred one itself.

Routes only some apps' traffic through the VPN.

SDK calls:
VPNProperties.Builder.withSplitTunneling(String[] packageNames)
VPNProperties.Builder.withReverseSplitTunneling(String[] packageNames)

How to use: pass the package names when building VPNProperties, before connect(). Split tunneling sends only the listed apps (plus your own app) through the VPN; reverse split tunneling keeps the listed apps off it.

Opens the SDK log.

SDK call:
AtomManager.addVPNStateListener(listener)

How to use: register a VPNStateListener once, for example in Application.onCreate(), and record its callbacks - onConnecting(), onConnected(), onDialError(), onDisconnected() and onStateChange().

Connection options applied to every connect().

SDK calls:
withAtomShield(TRACKER_AND_AD_BLOCKER)
allowLocalNetworkTraffic()
enableProtocolSwitch(boolean)
withUseFailoverEnabled(boolean)
withAutomaticPort() · withManualPort(int)
withServerFilter(List<ServerFilter>)
AtomConfiguration.Builder.persistVPNDetails(boolean)

How to use: set them on VPNProperties.Builder before connect(); persistVPNDetails goes on AtomConfiguration before initialize().

The ATOM SDK version this app is built against, and this app's build number.

SDK value:
de.blinkt.openvpn.BuildConfig.SDKVersion

Puts the VPN protocol, connection features and split tunneling back to their defaults, so the next VPNProperties is built without them.\n\nNo dedicated SDK call. AtomConfiguration options such as persistVPNDetails are only read by AtomManager.initialize(context, atomConfiguration, callback), so they change from the next launch.

Picks the country to dial. Only countries that support every selected protocol are listed.

SDK calls:
atomManager.getCountries(CollectionCallback)
new VPNProperties.Builder(country, primaryProtocol)

How to use: every Country carries getProtocols(); check it contains your protocols before dialling.

Picks a city inside the selected country. Optional - "Any city" dials the country itself.

SDK calls:
atomManager.getCities(CollectionCallback)
new VPNProperties.Builder(city, primaryProtocol)

How to use: filter getCities() by city.getCountry() and city.getProtocols(), then pass the City to the builder instead of the Country.

Picks the channel to dial. Only channels that support every selected protocol are listed.

SDK calls:
atomManager.getChannels(CollectionCallback)
new VPNProperties.Builder(channel, primaryProtocol)

How to use: every Channel carries getProtocols(); check it contains your protocols before dialling.

Adds another dedicated host, up to four. The SDK tries them in order until one connects.\n\nHow to use: build one DedicatedDNS per host with setDedicatedHostName(), setDedicatedHostIP(), setProtocol() and setPortNumber(), and pass the list to new VPNProperties.Builder(dedicatedDNSList, protocol).
The protocol this host is dialled with.\n\nHow to use: pick a Protocol from atomManager.getProtocols(CollectionCallback) and set it with dedicatedDNS.setProtocol(protocol).

The protocol to prefer across all hosts. Automatic passes null, so each host is dialled with its own protocol.

SDK call:
new VPNProperties.Builder(List<DedicatedDNS> dedicatedDNSList, Protocol protocol)

The protocol used for the dedicated IP. This demo dials dedicated hosts over IKEv2.\n\nHow to use: build it with protocol.setName(ProtocolName.IKEV) and protocol.setProtocol(ProtocolType.IKEV), then pass it to new VPNProperties.Builder(dedicatedHost, protocol).

The protocol tried first.

SDK calls:
atomManager.getProtocols(CollectionCallback)
new VPNProperties.Builder(location, primaryProtocol)

How to use: pick any Protocol from getProtocols(); it is required.

Fallback protocol if the primary one fails. Optional.

SDK call:
VPNProperties.Builder.withSecondaryProtocol(protocol)

How to use: add it to the builder before build(); the SDK retries with it when the primary protocol cannot connect.

Last fallback protocol, after the secondary one. Optional.

SDK call:
VPNProperties.Builder.withTertiaryProtocol(protocol)

How to use: add it to the builder before build(); the SDK tries it when both earlier protocols fail.

Dials the selected location. While connecting, the same button cancels.

SDK calls:
atomManager.setVPNCredentials(new VPNCredentials(username, password))
atomManager.connect(context, vpnProperties)
atomManager.cancel(context)

How to use: build VPNProperties with VPNProperties.Builder, then call connect(). Progress arrives on VPNStateListener: onConnecting(), then onConnected() or onDialError().

Drops the current connection, or cancels one still dialling.

SDK calls:
atomManager.disconnect(context)
atomManager.cancel(context)

How to use: disconnect() for a connected or paused tunnel, cancel() while getCurrentVpnStatus() is CONNECTING. Completion arrives on onDisconnected(connectionDetails).

Tears the tunnel down and dials the last connection again.

SDK call:
atomManager.reconnect(context)

How to use: needs a previous connection to repeat. An overload, reconnect(context, dialingType), also takes a DialingType.

Pauses the VPN for a chosen time; it resumes by itself when the timer ends.

SDK call:
atomManager.pause(PauseVPNTimer)

How to use: pass MINUTES_5, MINUTES_10, MINUTES_15, MINUTES_30, MINUTES_60, or MANUAL to stay paused until resume(). Only works while connected; onPaused() confirms it.

Resumes a paused VPN.

SDK call:
atomManager.resume()

How to use: call it while getCurrentVpnStatus() is PAUSED - required after pause(PauseVPNTimer.MANUAL).

Connection over Connection: switches to the selected location without disconnecting first.

No dedicated SDK call - it is connect() called while already connected or paused:
atomManager.connect(context, newVpnProperties)

How to use: pick a new location, then call connect(). The SDK keeps the new properties, disconnects the current tunnel and dials the new one; connectionDetails.isConnectionOverConnection() is true for it.
